**Brief: the notebook is 3 handwritten pages in Portuguese, dated "Aula 14/10". It covers one topic, the Binary Symmetric Channel (Canal Binário Simétrico), plus a worked probability example.**

**Page 1: theory (Aula 14/10)**
- The title is "Canal Binário Simétrico". The word "Canal" is circled and annotated "físico" (physical). (p. 1)
- The channel sends binary signals (0 and 1). When a 0 is sent, a 0 is expected at the receiver. (p. 1)
- Diagram: the transmitter "X" is on the left, with inputs 0 and 1. The receiver "Y" is on the right, with outputs 0 and 1. (p. 1)
  - The straight arrows 0→0 and 1→1 are each labeled **1 − pe**.
  - The crossed arrows 0→1 and 1→0 are each labeled **pe**. (p. 1)
- **pe = probabilidade de erro.** The word "prob." is circled and annotated "condicional". (p. 1)
- "Symmetry" is related to the probability of swapping 0 for 1 or 1 for 0. Both swaps have the same probability. (p. 1)
- Noise is the thing responsible for altering the 0s and 1s. This line is highlighted. (p. 1)
- A wave is formed by a sequence of 0s or 1s. In other words, each value is a piece of the wave. (p. 1)
- Formula: **pe = P(Y=0 | X=1) = P(Y=1 | X=0)**, where X = receptor (receiver) and Y = "desirnarcrio". (p. 1)
  - The Y label is hard to read. It is probably "destinatário" (destination).
  - The notebook writes X as the receiver. Given the diagram, X is more likely the transmitter and Y the receiver. The notebook's own labels are as quoted above.
- "Lembrete" (reminder) on probability: (p. 1)
  - **P(A,B) or P(A∩B)** is the joint probability. **P(A,B) = P(B)·P(A|B)**.
  - **P(A|B)** is the conditional probability: given that B occurred, the probability that A occurs.
  - **P(B|A) = P(B)·P(A|B) / P(A)** is the **Teorema de Bayes**.

**Page 2: example "canal binário simétrico", part (a)**
- The same diagram is drawn, with X on the left and Y on the right. (p. 2)
- Given: **pe = 0,1**, **P(X=0) = 0,6**, **P(X=1) = 0,4**. (p. 2)
- Asked:
  - (a) P(Y=0) and P(Y=1).
  - (b) P(X=0|Y=0) and P(X=1|Y=0). (p. 2)
- Method for (a): total probability. **P(Y=0) = P(X=0,Y=0) + P(X=1,Y=0)**. Each joint term is written as P(X)·P(Y|X). (p. 2)
- P(X=0,Y=0) = P(X=0)·P(Y=0|X=0) = 0,6 · 0,9 = **0,54**. Here 1 − pe = 1 − 0,1 = 0,9, which the notes call "probabilidade de não dar erro" (probability of no error). (p. 2)
- P(X=1,Y=0) = P(X=1)·P(Y=0|X=1) = 0,4 · 0,1 = **0,04**. (p. 2)
- Sum: 0,6·0,9 + 0,4·0,1 = **0,58**. (p. 2)
- Result (boxed): **P(Y=0) = 0,58** and **P(Y=1) = 1 − 0,58 = 0,42**. (p. 2)

**Page 3: part (b), posterior probabilities via Bayes**
- The page asks for four values: P(X=0|Y=0), P(X=1|Y=0), P(X=0|Y=1) and P(X=1|Y=1). (p. 3)
- **P(X=0|Y=0) = P(X=0)·P(Y=0|X=0) / P(Y=0) = 0,6·0,9 / 0,58 ≈ 0,93.** (p. 3)
- **P(X=1|Y=0) = 1 − P(X=0|Y=0) ≈ 1 − 0,93 = 0,07.** (p. 3)
- **P(X=0|Y=1) = P(X=0)·P(Y=1|X=0) / P(Y=1) = 0,6·0,1 / 0,42 ≈ 0,14.** Here P(Y=1|X=0) = pe = 0,1 and P(Y=1) = 0,42. (p. 3)
- **P(X=1|Y=1) = 1 − P(X=0|Y=1) ≈ 1 − 0,14 = 0,86.** (p. 3)
- The notes use the complement rule (the two posteriors for a given Y sum to 1) instead of applying Bayes a second time. (p. 3)
